answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bind each agent to a ferrous collateral ledger, where staking collateral and slashing penalties price duplicate identities above their marginal benefit. A verifiable delay function, modeled as a lagoon of sequential hashing, yields an information-theoretic unforgeability barrier because cloning would require inverting polynomial-time commitments and paying quadratic proof costs. Thus harbor consensus yields negative expected attack utility and a robust Nash equilibrium.
